# Exceptional cap corrections in a finite irreducible circuit

This note combines the proved section-normal classification with the
capwise logarithmic flux and the positive-convex defect budget. It gives
forced relations on actual exceptional-cap weights. It does not construct
a finite menu from a weak cap law, condition the physical separator on
arbitrary source groups, or prove defect vanishing.

Dependencies:

* `candidate 53c44db9ae559bfe`;
* `candidate 4dd22db8fd75566e`;
* `candidate 3432196fb93eb580`.

## 1. Fixed finite records and a single gradient

Retain one finite actual limiting cap law with positive weights
\(\theta_H\), summing to one, and all joint selectors and defects from
the dependencies. Suppose every surviving volume-gradient label equals
the same nonzero vector (c\). The original-volume row mixture then
implies that, in each sampled fiber,

\[
 L(z,X)=\ell(z)+c\cdot X.
\]

Indeed its continuous gradient is (c\) almost everywhere in each
fiber, and continuity gives the displayed affine restriction. The
limiting touching planes at uniformly interior sources have the same
continuous gradient. If (c=0\), these restrictions are positive constants
and there is no zero set or defect; below (c\ne0\).

Let (zeta\) be the total inverse-volume defect and (zeta^H\) its
actual part captured by cap (H\). Let (a_H\) be its boundary cap-load
defect, (s_H\) its section-log defect, and (b\) the whole boundary
defect. The exact identities and domination are

\[
 -\pi_*(n b)=Mc\zeta,\qquad
 -\pi_*(n a_H)=Mc\zeta^H-u_Hs_H,
 \quad0\le a_H\le b,\quad0\le\zeta^H\le\zeta.       \tag{1}
\]

For (a=\sum_H\theta_Ha_H\) and the SAME quadratic reserve (q\ge0\),

\[
 \int\psi(n)f(w)\,d(a+q)
 \le\beta\int\psi(n)f(w)\,db                        \tag{2}
\]

for every continuous nonnegative (psi\) and every nonnegative finite
convex (f\). No selector in (1) or (2) is replaced by a limiting closed
halfspace bit.

The normal classification implies

\[
 s_H\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u_H\parallel c.   \tag{3}
\]

At every fiber carrying this defect, the cap plane is the zero support
plane of (L\). If (u_H=k_Hc\), the limiting incidence is inside for
(k_H>0\), and outside for (k_H<0\). Both are possible.

Assume for now that the continuous normals of this law form an
irreducible positive circuit of full rank (d\ge2\). There is at most
one index (E\) whose normal is parallel to (c\). Repeated rays would
allow one repeated vector to be deleted and its positive coefficient
added to the other. Opposite rays already form a positive dependence
on a proper subcollection. Both contradict irreducibility.

Consequently the section correction

\[
 \sum_H\theta_Hu_Hs_H=\theta_Eu_Es_E               \tag{4}
\]

cannot cancel internally unless (s_E=0\). This is equality of vector
measures, not just of their total masses. The statement explicitly
assumes the limiting circuit remains irreducible and full rank; that
does not follow merely from prelimit irreducibility.

## 2. A general projected variation inequality

Put (e=c/|c|\) and

\[
 \zeta^{\rm cap}=\sum_H\theta_H\zeta^H,\qquad
 B_e(f)=\int |e\cdot n|f\,db,\quad
 Q_e(f)=\int |e\cdot n|f\,dq.
\]

If there is an exceptional cap, write
\(\varepsilon_E=\operatorname{sgn}(u_E\cdot c)\).
If there is none, omit the following section term. Equation (1) gives
the signed scalar-measure identity

\[
 M|c|\zeta^{\rm cap}
 -\theta_E\varepsilon_E|u_E|s_E
       =-\pi_*((e\cdot n)a).
\]

Total variation of a pushforward satisfies
\(|\pi_*((e\cdot n)a)|\le\pi_*(|e\cdot n|a)\).
Apply (2) with (psi=|e\cdot n|\). For EVERY nonnegative convex (f\),

\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \int f\,d\left|M|c|\zeta^{\rm cap}
          -\theta_E\varepsilon_E|u_E|s_E\right|
       +Q_e(f)\le\beta B_e(f).
       \quad}                                      \tag{5}
\]

This retains spatial cancellation correctly; it is stronger than taking
only the absolute value of the integrated scalar. In particular, with
(Z_f^{\rm cap}=\int f\,d\zeta^{\rm cap}\) and (S_f=\int f\,ds_E\),

\[
 \left|M|c|Z_f^{\rm cap}
       -\theta_E\varepsilon_E|u_E|S_f\right|
       \le\beta B_e(f)-Q_e(f).                    \tag{6}
\]

If the exception is absent or outside, all measures inside the absolute
value in (5) are nonnegative. Thus

\[
 M|c|Z_f^{\rm cap}
 +\mathbf1_{\{E\text{ outside}\}}\theta_E|u_E|S_f
       +Q_e(f)\le\beta B_e(f).                    \tag{7}
\]

An outside exception cannot compensate an excess captured inverse
defect. An inside exception must pay at least

\[
 \theta_E|u_E|S_f
 \ge [M|c|Z_f^{\rm cap}-\beta B_e(f)+Q_e(f)]_+.    \tag{8}
\]

The individual cap flux and (a_E\le b\) also give

\[
 |u_E|S_f\le M|c|\int f\,d\zeta^E+B_e(f).
\]

Therefore every inside exception satisfies the concrete weight bound

\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \theta_E\ge
 \frac{[M|c|Z_f^{\rm cap}-\beta B_e(f)+Q_e(f)]_+}
      {M|c|\int f\,d\zeta^E+B_e(f)}.
 \quad}                                           \tag{9}
\]

When the denominator is zero, the numerator and relevant defect masses
are zero, so that test is vacuous. No common affine core or angle bound
for the boundary normals was used in (5)–(9).

## 3. A sharper radial identity when an affine interior core is available

Suppose there is an affine continuous graph (g(z)\) lying uniformly in
the interior of every fiber carrying (b\). It may be arbitrary on the
other fibers. Define

\[
 r(n,z,X)=(n\cdot(X-g(z)))_+,
 \quad h_z=L(z,g(z))>0
\]

on the relevant bases. On the defect's actual normal bundle, (r\) is
the strictly positive support distance. The test is convex in physical
variables for each normal. Inequality (2) extends to this test by a
finite nonnegative continuous partition of unity on the normal sphere:
freeze its normal argument in each convex test and take uniform limits
on the common compact set. No unsigned affine test is inserted into
the positive-convex order.

Testing (1) with the affine-in-(X\) field (X-g(z)\) gives

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 B&:=\int r\,db=M\int h_z\,d\zeta,\\
 B_H&:=\int r\,da_H
       =M\int h_z\,d\zeta^H
          -k_H\int h_z\,ds_H\quad (u_H=k_Hc).
 \end{aligned}                                    \tag{10}
\]

For a nonexceptional cap the section term is zero. The identities use
(c\cdot(X-g(z))=-h_z\) on the zero set and
(u_H\cdot(X-g(z))=-k_Hh_z\) on the exceptional section defect.
They do not infer a boundary/volume coupling from equality of totals.

If (B=0\), all these defects vanish. Otherwise put

\[
 t_H=\frac{M\int h_z\,d\zeta^H}{B}\in[0,1],\quad
 r_E=\frac{|k_E|\int h_z\,ds_E}{B},\quad
 q_r=\frac{\int r\,dq}{B}\ge0.
\]

Since (0\le B_H\le B\), (10) yields the exact status rules

\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{status}&B_H/B&\text{necessary range}\\\hline
 \text{nonexceptional}&t_H&0\le t_H\le1\\
 \text{inside exception}&t_E-r_E&0\le r_E\le t_E\\
 \text{outside exception}&t_E+r_E&0\le r_E\le1-t_E.
 \end{array}                                       \tag{11}
\]

The full law satisfies

\[
 \sum_H\theta_Ht_H-\theta_E\varepsilon_Er_E+q_r
       \le\beta.                                  \tag{12}
\]

In particular a single inside exception can hide **at most its own**
captured inverse-defect mass. Irrespective of its section allocation,

\[
 \sum_{H\ne E}\theta_Ht_H+q_r\le\beta.            \tag{13}
\]

An outside exception satisfies the stronger
(\sum_H\theta_Ht_H+q_r\le\beta\). If (t_E>0\), an inside exception
also requires

\[
 \theta_E\ge
 \frac{[\sum_H\theta_Ht_H+q_r-\beta]_+}{t_E}.      \tag{14}
\]

These relations do not bound (t_H\) by a closed-halfspace indicator at
a zero point lying on that cap plane. That allocation remains actual.

## 4. A planar atomic incidence consequence

Suppose additionally (d=2\), all boundary/inverse defect is supported
over one physical zero point (w_*=(z_*,x_*)\), and there is one
exceptional cap (E\). An affine (g\) as needed above can be chosen
constant, using any interior point of (K_{z_*}\); no condition on
other fibers is then needed.

Let the three actual cap margins (m_H(w)\) have a positive circuit
(\rho_H\), and assume their weighted cover margin is zero at (w_*\):

\[
 \sum_H\rho_Hm_H(w_*)=0.
\]

This is the actual fixed-face relation, not a consequence of the
continuous normal balance at an arbitrary base. The exceptional margin
is zero by the zero-plane classification. If both other margins are
nonzero, their signs must be opposite. Call the strictly capturing cap
(C\) and the strictly missing cap (D\).

The corresponding actual defect restrictions are (t_C=1\), (t_D=0\):
strict incidence persists throughout a neighborhood of the limiting
atom and along the prelimit records. Equation (13) then gives

\[
 \boxed{\ \theta_C+q_r\le\beta.\ }                \tag{15}
\]

For an outside exception, (12) only strengthens this requirement.
Thus a generic atomic exceptional incidence cannot coexist with a
strictly capturing other cap whose weight exceeds ( eta\). This is
a specific incidence/weight constraint; no universal lower bound on
that particular cap weight is assumed. If another cap also passes
through (w_*\), its defect fraction must be retained and (15) need
not follow.

## 5. Why ordinary section balance does not remove the correction

Every nonzero section defect in this setting has vanishing unweighted
coarea. Hence it contributes zero to the limiting section masses and
first moments used in the ordinary source-section centroid/balance
identities. Its logarithmically weighted mass can nevertheless survive.

The actual truncated-triangle sequence in the section-classification
note makes this explicit. For the inside proper caps
(x+y\ge a+\eta^2\), the limiting defect data are

\[
 b=\sqrt2\log2\,\delta_{(n_0,0)},\quad
 M c\zeta=(\log2,\log2)\delta_0,\quad
 a_H=0,\quad\zeta^H=\zeta,\quad s_H=\log2\,\delta_0.
\]

The capwise terms cancel exactly: (Mc\zeta-u s_H=0\).
In (11) this is (t_H=r_H=1\), attaining the inside upper bound.
For the complementary proper caps, (zeta^{H^c}=0\),
(a_{H^c}=b\), the same (s_H\) remains, and (11) has
(t_{H^c}=0,r_{H^c}=1\), attaining the outside bound.

Equal weights on these two actual complementary records cancel their
section vectors, as a rank-one opposite pair permits. This calibration
is cap-realized but is **not** asserted to be a critical/deepest-source
circuit. It proves the status bounds are geometrically sharp and that
vanishing ordinary coarea alone is not a cancellation argument.

For (d\ge2\), (4) prevents this opposite-pair cancellation within an
irreducible full-rank group. Several different groups can still have
opposite exceptional rays and can cancel after mixing.

## 6. Conditioning limitations

The defect budget (2) belongs to the SAME full physical cap law. It
cannot automatically be imposed on each group after splitting that
law. Equations (5)–(15) apply when the whole law is the stated single
group, or when the corresponding conditional budget is separately
proved. The geometric assertion (4) itself applies group by group.

Likewise the inverse-volume defects have source-gradient labels, but
the boundary defect (b\) has not been split into positive labeled
measures with the same flux. Splitting finite-PL gradient cells in a
divergence formula creates internal interface terms. The finite list
of exceptional section normals does not supply the missing labeled
surface disintegration.

Thus generic irreducible groups do not admit an internal cancellation
of their sole exceptional section correction. The surviving quantitative
information is (5), and, under the explicit radial hypothesis, (11)–(15).
Neither conditioning nor an OC payment is inferred from these facts.
